_about: Authored words for all-endpoints.html — the only strings on the page that are not facts. gen-all-endpoints.py refuses to build when a line here types a number (a {token} the generator or the page fills instead) or says a word D-018 took out. Tokens the generator fills are listed in its `tok`; the ones the page fills while it runs are listed in _runtime.
eyebrow: every endpoint of one app, side by side
h1: All {nRows} endpoints of {app}, one row each
lede: Each row is one endpoint. Each column is one attribute of the endpoint card, set under the card's {nBlocks} ruled blocks, so you read a column top to bottom to see a pattern. The small strip under every column header shows how that column's values spread over all {nRows} rows.
proposal: This page is a proposal. Which attributes became columns, how each is drawn, and every way of grouping the rows are my picks. Each choice is on the rail below with my pick marked, so you can change it by looking.
stamp: {app} at head {head} · {nFeed} endpoints in its feed
partial: A fixture page, not the app's page: it draws {nRows} of the feed's {nFeed} endpoints.
keys: Click a column header to sort by it, again to reverse it. Click a piece of a header strip to light the rows in it. Click a row for everything it holds.

rows.name: one per row
rows.plain: A dense table: one endpoint per line, every column lined up.

two.name: {cards} per row
two.plain: Small cards, {cards} across, each holding the same cells as a row.

three.name: {cards} per row
three.plain: Small cards, {cards} across, each holding the same cells as a row.

entity.name: entity
entity.plain: The entity that claims the endpoint, from the claim registry.

seg.name: first URL segment
seg.plain: The first part of the path, the way the URL groups it.

method.name: method
method.plain: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE apart.

labels.name: ending labels
labels.plain: Endpoints whose endings carry the same stage and status labels sit together. A clone shows up as a group.

counts.name: ending counts
counts.plain: Endpoints with the same count in every kind of ending sit together. Coarser than the labels.

flat.name: no groups
flat.plain: One list, sorted by whatever column you pick.

alone.label: a group of a single endpoint

gather.name: gathered at the end
gather.plain: Every group that holds a single endpoint is drawn together under one header at the bottom.

own.name: its own header
own.plain: Every group gets its own header, even with a single endpoint in it.

size.name: largest first
size.plain: The group with the most endpoints on top.

own.name: their own group, first
own.plain: An attribute several blocks need is homed in none of them by the ruled tree, so these columns stand in a group of their own, before the blocks.

first.name: under the first block
first.plain: A shared attribute is drawn under the first block, in the current block order, that needs it.

stage.name: stage order
stage.plain: Blocks in the brain map's stage order: a block sits by the first stage its list names, from the edge to the answer, and blocks that name no stage come last.

card.name: the card's order
card.plain: Blocks in the order the ruled tree lists them.

all.name: every column
all.plain: Every column I drew, including the ones the inventory rates below the top, which I kept because a pattern needs them. Their headers say their rating.

top.name: rated {rTop} only
top.plain: Only attributes the inventory rates {rTop}, the face of the card.

heat.name: tinted by size
heat.plain: A number's cell is tinted by its value against the largest in its column, so a column reads as a picture.

quiet.name: drawn quiet
quiet.plain: In a column of names, the value most endpoints share is a faint dot, and every other value is written out, so the odd one speaks.

full.name: written out
full.plain: Every value written out, the common one too.

pickPlain: The option I would choose alone. Yours to change.
sortHint: Click to sort by this column, again to reverse.
rating: rated {rating} of {top} in the card's inventory
alarmRating: an alert attribute: drawn only when something is abnormal
stripHint: Click to light these rows, again to clear.
absentWhy: The feed carries no reading for this: {why}. This is not a zero.

group.sum: added up over the group's endpoints: each one's own, so nothing is counted twice
group.union: distinct across the group's endpoints: a thing several of them share is counted once
group.has: endpoints in the group that have one
group.ratio: endings proven on their own over all endings, added up over the group's endpoints

sharedBlock.name: Shared
sharedBlock.plain: Attributes that several of the card's blocks need. The ruled tree homes them in none of those blocks.

blockEmpty: Nothing in this block is rated {top}, so it is hidden while the rail shows only those columns.

stages.EDGE: the app band, before the endpoint is reached
stages.INPUT: the input is read and checked against its shape
stages.EFFECTS: the writes left behind; no ending leaves from here
stages.ANSWER: the reply goes back; every success leaves here
stages.UNCAUGHT: anything nobody caught, the bay beside every stage

success.name: success
success.plain: An ending the endpoint means to reach.

refusal.name: refusal
refusal.plain: An ending where the app's own code says no.

framework.name: framework
framework.plain: An ending the framework produces while it reads the body, before any code of the app runs.

validation.name: validation
validation.plain: The ending where the input, the body, the query, the path or a header, does not fit its declared shape.

saved.name: saved
saved.plain: The path commits the endpoint's own writes.

maybe.name: maybe saved
maybe.plain: A write is committed on some turns of the path and not on others.

rolled.name: rolled back
rolled.plain: The path rolls the endpoint's writes back.

unsaved.name: left unsaved
unsaved.plain: The path leaves a write that nothing commits.

after.name: after the answer
after.plain: The path's own writes run after the reply has started, in the code that streams it.

none.name: no own write
none.plain: The path writes nothing of its own. The login check's writes are the gate's, named apart in the side panel.

the norm.name: the norm
the norm.plain: A piece nearly every endpoint of the app carries.

only here.name: only here
only here.plain: A piece no other endpoint of the app carries.

all.head: endings
all.name: every way a request can end
all.zero: the feed lists no ending for it

stage.head: stages
stage.name: the stages its endings leave from, edge to answer, with the uncaught bay apart
stage.zero: no ending leaves from any stage

guards.head: guards
guards.name: checks in its own code that refuse the request
guards.zero: its own code holds no check that refuses

auth.head: login
auth.name: the login scheme it asks for

response.head: reply
response.name: fields in the body a success answers with
response.unknown: It answers with {model}, and how many fields that has is unknown. This is not a zero.

e_success.head: ok
e_success.name: success endings
e_success.zero: the feed read no success ending

e_framework.head: body
e_framework.name: endings the framework produces while it reads the body
e_framework.zero: it reads no body, so the framework cannot refuse one

e_validation.head: shape
e_validation.name: the ending where its input does not fit its declared shape: the body, the query, the path or a header

e_uncaught.head: uncaught
e_uncaught.name: uncaught endings
e_uncaught.zero: the feed read no uncaught ending

acts.head: tests
acts.name: tests that call it to test it
acts.zero: no test calls it to test it

asserted.head: beyond
asserted.name: proofs that check more than the status code
asserted.zero: every proof checks the status code alone, or there is no proof

branches.head: forks
branches.name: branches in called code that change how it ends
branches.zero: no called branch changes the ending

catches.head: catches
catches.name: try and except blocks on its paths

rate.head: rate
rate.name: the rate limiters it sits behind

written.head: writes
written.name: tables its own code writes; a table only the login check writes is left out
written.zero: its own code writes no table

fate.head: fate
fate.name: its paths, by what becomes of the endpoint's own writes; the number is the paths that save
fate.zero: no path saves a write of its own before the answer

deciders.head: deciders
deciders.name: functions whose refusal or raise becomes one of its endings
deciders.zero: no function's refusal becomes an ending here

datafns.head: data fns
datafns.name: functions that read or write the database on its own paths
datafns.zero: none of its own functions touches the database

request.head: fields
request.name: fields at the top of the JSON body it reads
request.unknown: It reads a JSON body, and how many fields that body has is unknown. This is not a zero.

fetched.head: screen
fetched.name: frontend hooks that call it
fetched.zero: no screen of the app calls it

reasons.head: reads
reasons.name: places in the frontend that read its status, detail or code
reasons.zero: no screen reads why it refused

cases422.head: rules
cases422.name: rules on its input, body, query, path or headers, that make it fail with a 422

inf_answer.head: request
inf_answer.name: values alive only while the request runs, gone with the answer
inf_answer.zero: nothing lives only for the request

inf_server.head: server
inf_server.name: values the server process keeps between requests
inf_server.zero: nothing is kept by the process

proof.head: proven
proof.name: endings a test proves on its own, of all its endings; a test whose status fits several endings proves none of them
proof.zero: no test proves any of its endings on its own
proof.amb: {amb} more endings only by a test whose status fits several

behind.head: behind
behind.name: functions reachable behind its handler
behind.zero: the map reaches no function behind it

switches.head: switches
switches.name: settings or swapped-in parts that change what it does

pieces.head: pieces
pieces.name: its pieces by how common each is in the app; the number is the rare ones plus the ones only it has
pieces.zero: every piece it has is common or the norm

lacks.head: lacks
lacks.name: pieces nearly every endpoint carries that it does not
lacks.zero: it carries every piece that is the norm

families: the form check's findings, one place each, most frequent first

panel.proofWords: {n} of its refusals named by a test, a test that fits several counted for each · rank {v} of {of}
panel.labPlain: The lab is baked to one endpoint today. These commands bake it to this endpoint; they rewrite the lab's own facts file, so run them only when you mean to move the lab here.

more.show: Show how the map knows this
lines: Every row comes from the lab's own reader: gen-endpoint-facts.py ran once per endpoint, into a temporary file, never over the lab's facts. This page keeps a small record of each and counts what the facts already say.
The feed is the forms file of {app} at head {head}, sha {formsSha}, with its map beside it, sha {archmapSha}. Arms on: {arms}. Arms off: {armsOff}.
A cell that reads absent means the feed did not look. A cell that reads unknown means it looked, and the value is not known. A zero means it looked and found nothing, and its hover says why.

The stage an ending leaves from follows the robot's lay: the app band's endings at the edge, the login check's at the gate, the body's at the input, the endpoint's own refusals in the handler, every success at the answer, and the uncaught in the bay.

The writes column and a path's fate read the endpoint's own writes only. The login check can create a user row on almost every endpoint; counting it would paint both columns the same, so the side panel names those writes apart, as the login check's.

copy.intro: What you are looking at, as text, to paste back with your words under it.

authNoSchemePlain: It asks for a login through its own check, with no declared scheme: the check reads the token itself, not from the usual header.
